judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 172, which required Ohio public offices and public officials to allow the arrest or detention of any person unlawfully present in the United States for deportation or other immigration proceedings, anywhere in the state and despite the privilege from arrest that continuing law grants in certain cases. It passed the Ohio Senate 23-8.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing S.B. 172, which required Ohio public offices and public officials to allow the arrest or detention of any person unlawfully present in the United States for deportation or other immigration proceedings, anywhere in the state and despite the privilege from arrest that continuing law grants in certain cases. It passed the Ohio Senate 23-8.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 293, which required absentee ballots returned by mail to reach the board of elections by the 7:30 p.m. close of polls on Election Day to be counted, ending the four-day grace period, and directed monthly checks of state and federal databases to cancel the registrations of people identified as noncitizens. It passed the Ohio House 61-30 and was signed into law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing S.B. 293, which required absentee ballots returned by mail to reach the board of elections by the 7:30 p.m. close of polls on Election Day to be counted, ending the four-day grace period, and directed monthly checks of state and federal databases to cancel the registrations of people identified as noncitizens. It passed the Ohio House 61-30 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to concur in House amendments to S.B. 293, sending to the Governor a law that required absentee ballots returned by mail to reach the board of elections by the 7:30 p.m. close of polls on Election Day to be counted, ending the four-day grace period, and directed monthly database checks to cancel the registrations of people identified as noncitizens. It passed the Ohio Senate 23-10 and was signed into law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against concurring in House amendments to S.B. 293, which sent to the Governor a law that required absentee ballots returned by mail to reach the board of elections by the 7:30 p.m. close of polls on Election Day to be counted, ending the four-day grace period, and directed monthly database checks to cancel the registrations of people identified as noncitizens. It passed the Ohio Senate 23-10 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 88, which increased the penalties for trafficking cocaine, fentanyl-related compounds, heroin, and methamphetamine, removed the knowledge requirement for certain fentanyl possession offenses, and required public schools to teach students in kindergarten through grade 12 about the dangers of fentanyl. It passed the Ohio House 71-18.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 88, which increased the penalties for trafficking cocaine, fentanyl-related compounds, heroin, and methamphetamine, removed the knowledge requirement for certain fentanyl possession offenses, and required public schools to teach students in kindergarten through grade 12 about the dangers of fentanyl. It passed the Ohio House 71-18.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 485, the Baby Olivia Act, which required every public school to teach human growth and development in grades 5 through 12 using a high-definition ultrasound video and the "Meet Baby Olivia" video produced by the anti-abortion group Live Action, or a substantially similar video. It passed the Ohio House 59-27.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 485, the Baby Olivia Act, which required every public school to teach human growth and development in grades 5 through 12 using a high-definition ultrasound video and the "Meet Baby Olivia" video produced by the anti-abortion group Live Action, or a substantially similar video. It passed the Ohio House 59-27.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 492, which expanded the offense of interfering with an officer arresting someone for a traffic or vehicle equipment violation and raised its penalty, and created a new offense for a driver or passenger who refused to give their name, address, or birthdate to an officer investigating certain motor-vehicle violations. It passed the Ohio House 59-21 and was signed into law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 492, which expanded the offense of interfering with an officer arresting someone for a traffic or vehicle equipment violation and raised its penalty, and created a new offense for a driver or passenger who refused to give their name, address, or birthdate to an officer investigating certain motor-vehicle violations. It passed the Ohio House 59-21 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 492, which expanded the offense of interfering with an officer arresting someone for a traffic or vehicle equipment violation and raised its penalty, and created a new offense for a driver or passenger who refused to give their name, address, or birthdate to an officer investigating certain motor-vehicle violations. It passed the Ohio Senate 24-9 and was signed into law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 492, which expanded the offense of interfering with an officer arresting someone for a traffic or vehicle equipment violation and raised its penalty, and created a new offense for a driver or passenger who refused to give their name, address, or birthdate to an officer investigating certain motor-vehicle violations. It passed the Ohio Senate 24-9 and was signed into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 249, the Indecent Exposure Modernization Act, which created the criminal offense of unlawful adult cabaret performance for performances outside an adult cabaret that are harmful to juveniles or obscene, a category the bill defined to include entertainers who exhibit a gender identity different from their biological sex. It passed the Ohio House 63-32.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 249, the Indecent Exposure Modernization Act, which created the criminal offense of unlawful adult cabaret performance for performances outside an adult cabaret that are harmful to juveniles or obscene, a category the bill defined to include entertainers who exhibit a gender identity different from their biological sex. It passed the Ohio House 63-32.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 252, which created new aggravated burglary, burglary, and trespass offenses that dropped the requirement that the offender act by force, stealth, or deception, and generally increased the penalties for the existing offenses. It passed the Ohio House 70-25.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 252, which created new aggravated burglary, burglary, and trespass offenses that dropped the requirement that the offender act by force, stealth, or deception, and generally increased the penalties for the existing offenses. It passed the Ohio House 70-25.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 347, the SHE WINS Act, which permitted an elective abortion only where a physician met with the woman at least 24 hours beforehand to provide specified information and document her informed consent, and authorized civil damages and professional discipline against physicians who did not comply. It passed the Ohio House 64-32.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.B. 347, the SHE WINS Act, which permitted an elective abortion only where a physician met with the woman at least 24 hours beforehand to provide specified information and document her informed consent, and authorized civil damages and professional discipline against physicians who did not comply. It passed the Ohio House 64-32.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 278, which expanded the damages available against a municipal corporation that enacts or enforces gun control measures to include punitive or exemplary damages. It passed the Ohio Senate 24-9.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing S.B. 278, which expanded the damages available against a municipal corporation that enacts or enforces gun control measures to include punitive or exemplary damages. It passed the Ohio Senate 24-9.
